question: Your extraction system sends each financial filing to a separate subagent, and each subagent returns the extracted revenue figures as JSON to a synthesis agent. The synthesis agent merges these figures into one comparison report. Reviewers find that the report mixes quarterly and annual figures and puts values from amended filings beside superseded ones. The reviewers also cannot trace any figure back to its page. Which change best addresses the root cause?

options.text: Pass the full text of every source filing to the synthesis agent along with the subagent outputs, so that it can check each figure against the original documents.
options.reason: This floods the synthesis agent's context with verbose content and risks lost-in-the-middle omissions. The guide says upstream agents should return structured key facts instead of verbose content.

options.text: Require each subagent's JSON output to include metadata for every figure, such as the reporting period, the filing date, and the source page and section.
options.reason: The guide says subagents should include metadata such as dates, source locations and methodological context in structured outputs, so that downstream synthesis is accurate and traceable.

options.text: Add an instruction to the synthesis agent's system prompt that tells it to separate quarterly figures from annual figures carefully when it merges them.
options.reason: The synthesis agent never receives the period, date or source data it would need. A prompt instruction cannot restore metadata that the subagent outputs lack.

options.text: Have each subagent return a short prose summary of its filing instead of JSON, so that the synthesis agent receives more readable input.
options.reason: The guide warns that summaries condense dates and numerical values into vague text. Prose also removes the structure that downstream synthesis needs.
